questions.q: Who defined physical education as 'the sum of changes in the individual caused by experiences centering in motor activity'?
questions.explanation: Rosalind Cassidy's definition focuses on the sum of changes caused by motor activity.

questions.q: In ancient Greece, what was the primary aim of the Spartan education system (Agoge)?
questions.explanation: Sparta focused entirely on creating fierce military warriors.

questions.q: In which year was the YMCA College of Physical Education established in Madras by H.C. Buck?
questions.explanation: H.C. Buck founded the YMCA College in 1920, marking the start of modern PE in India.

questions.q: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.qPa: ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਸਰੀਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਲੰਬੀ ਹੱਡੀ ਕਿਹੜੀ ਹੈ?
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone.

questions.q: Pushing against a solid wall is an example of which type of muscle contraction?
questions.explanation: Isometric contractions involve generating force without changing muscle length.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The Pulmonary Artery is the only artery that carries deoxygenated blood.

questions.q: Which gland is known as the 'Master Gland'?
questions.qPa: ਕਿਸ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ ਨੂੰ 'ਮਾਸਟਰ ਗ੍ਰੰਥੀ' ਕਿਹਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ?
questions.explanation: The Pituitary Gland controls the functions of many other endocrine glands.

questions.q: Where does the maximum absorption of nutrients occur in the human body?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is lined with villi specifically designed for maximum nutrient absorption.

questions.q: According to Thorndike's Law of Effect, a behavior is strengthened if followed by:
questions.explanation: Positive outcomes (rewards) strengthen the connection between stimulus and response.

questions.q: A coach who makes all decisions without consulting the team is exhibiting which leadership style?
questions.explanation: Autocratic leaders retain all decision-making power.

questions.q: A 'Paidotribe' in ancient Greece was a:
questions.explanation: A Paidotribe was a physical trainer or teacher.

questions.q: The Sports Authority of India (SAI) was established in:
questions.explanation: SAI was established in 1984 to promote sports and manage infrastructure.

questions.q: The maximum volume of air exhaled after a maximal inhalation is called:
questions.explanation: Vital Capacity measures the maximum usable capacity of the lungs.

questions.q: Which part of the brain is responsible for balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements and maintains balance.

questions.q: What is the functional filtering unit of the kidney?
questions.explanation: The nephron is the microscopic unit that filters blood to form urine.

questions.q: Which educational philosophy emphasizes 'learning by doing'?
questions.explanation: Pragmatism, championed by John Dewey, focuses on practical, experiential learning.

questions.q: Playing a sport purely for personal enjoyment rather than for a medal is an example of:
questions.qPa: ਮੈਡਲ ਦੀ ਬਜਾਏ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਨਿੱਜੀ ਆਨੰਦ ਲਈ ਖੇਡ ਖੇਡਣਾ ਕਿਸਦੀ ਉਦਾਹਰਣ ਹੈ?
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes from within the individual for the love of the activity itself.

questions.q: The knee joint is an example of a:
questions.explanation: The knee acts as a hinge, primarily allowing flexion and extension.

questions.q: Which hormone prepares the body for a 'fight or flight' response?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline (epinephrine) increases heart rate and blood flow during emergencies.

questions.q: Bile is produced by the:
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, which is then stored in the gallbladder.

questions.q: The degree to which team members work together to achieve a specific goal is called:
questions.explanation: Task cohesion focuses on performance and goal attainment.

questions.q: Cardiac muscle tissue is found only in the:
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is the specialized, involuntary muscle tissue of the heart.

questions.q: Who was the first president of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)?
questions.explanation: Sir Dorabji Tata was elected as the first president of the IOA in 1927.

questions.q: Cardiac output is calculated by multiplying Heart Rate by:
questions.explanation: Cardiac Output = Heart Rate × Stroke Volume.

questions.q: The phrase 'big muscle activities' is strongly associated with the definition of PE by:
questions.explanation: Voltmer and Esslinger defined PE as dealing with big muscle activities.
